title: A Day at the Market
text: On Saturday, Lina goes to the market with her mother. They bring a big bag. A man there sells cheese. Lina asks about the price. “Three dollars,” he says. He takes a knife and cuts a small piece for her to try. It is soft and very good. Lina smiles, and they buy some. Then they walk home in the sun.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “price” mean?
options: a prize you win in a game
the money you pay to buy something
the bag you carry food in
qs.why: The man answers “Three dollars,” so the price is the money you pay. “A prize” only sounds a little like the word.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “piece” mean?
options: a part cut off from something bigger
qs.why: He cuts a small part off the cheese for her to try. “A time with no fighting” is “peace,” a different word that sounds the same.

qs.q: Why does the man cut a small piece of cheese?
options: because the cheese is too big for the bag
so Lina can taste it before they buy
so he can eat it himself
so he can sell it for three dollars
qs.why: He cuts it “for her to try,” and after tasting it they buy some. Three dollars is the price he names, not the reason for cutting.

title: Max the Puppy
text: Omar has a new dog called Max. Max is small and has soft hair. Every morning, Omar and Max walk to the park together. Max runs after birds but never catches one. At night, Max will not sleep in his own bed. He jumps up next to Omar. Then he makes funny little noises in his dreams, and Omar laughs.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “hair” mean?
options: the soft stuff that grows on his body
qs.why: Max is a dog, and his soft hair is what grows on his body. “A small rabbit” is “hare,” a word that only sounds the same.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “funny” mean?
qs.why: Omar laughs at the noises, so they make him want to laugh. “Funny” can also mean strange, but here Omar is not worried.

qs.q: Where does Max sleep at night?
qs.why: Max will not sleep in his own bed; he jumps up next to Omar. A careless reader may pick “in his own bed.”

title: Saving for a Bike
text: Priya wants a red bike. The cost is 120 dollars. Each week, she helps her neighbor in the garden and gets ten dollars. She does not spend it. She saves it. Every month, her dad takes her to the bank to put the money in. After twelve weeks, she counts the amount she has: 120 dollars! Finally, she can buy the bike.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “saves” mean?
qs.why: She does not spend the money; she keeps it for the bike. “Save” can also mean to help someone out of danger, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “amount” mean?
qs.why: She counts how much money she has, and it is 120 dollars. “A big hill” is a mount, which only looks similar.

qs.q: How does Priya get the money for the bike?
options: her dad gives it to her
the bank gives it as a gift
she finds it in the garden
she wins it in a race
by helping her neighbor each week
qs.why: She gets ten dollars each week for helping in her neighbor's garden. Her dad only takes her to the bank.

title: Sunday Football
text: Every Sunday, Tom watches football on TV with his grandpa. Their team is in a big league with many other teams. Tom's favorite player is very fast. Today, he catches the ball and runs all the way down the field. Everyone jumps up and shouts. At the end, their team beats the other team, 21 to 14. Grandpa gives Tom a high five.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “league” mean?
options: a group of sports teams that play each other
qs.why: Their team is in a group “with many other teams” that play each other. It is not one game or one place.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “beats” mean?
options: makes a sound like a drum
qs.why: The score is 21 to 14 for their team, so it wins against the other team. A heart or drum “beats” too, but that is a different meaning.

qs.q: Which team wins the game?
options: no team, it is a tie
qs.why: Their team beats the other team 21 to 14, and Grandpa gives Tom a high five.

title: Ana's Arm
text: Ana falls off her bike and has pain in her arm. Her dad takes her to the hospital. The staff are very kind to her. A doctor looks at her arm. It is not broken. For treatment, she gets ice and a soft wrap. “Rest your arm for a few days,” the doctor says. One week later, Ana is fine and back on her bike.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “treatment” mean?
options: care from a doctor to help her get better
a long wait in a line
qs.why: The doctor gives her ice and a soft wrap so her arm can get better. A “sweet gift” is a treat, a different word.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “fine” mean?
options: money you pay for breaking a rule
qs.why: A week later Ana is back on her bike, so she is well. “Fine” can also mean money you pay for breaking a rule, but not here.

qs.q: What is wrong with Ana's arm?
options: it is broken in two places
nothing at all, it never hurt
it hurts, but it is not broken
she cannot move it for a year
qs.why: She has pain, but the doctor says it is not broken. She only needs ice, a wrap, and rest.

title: Summer on the Island
text: Every summer, Kenji and his family travel to a small island. They go by boat, and the trip across the sea takes two hours. There, they climb a tall hill. From the top, the view is beautiful. Kenji can see blue water all around him. He takes a photo to send to his grandma.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “view” mean?
options: what you can see from a place
qs.why: From the top of the hill, Kenji sees blue water all around. That is what you can see from a place. “View” can also mean an idea, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “travel” mean?
options: go from one place to another
qs.why: The family goes from home to the island by boat. They do not stay home.

qs.q: How does Kenji's family get to the island?
qs.why: The passage says “They go by boat,” and the trip is across the sea. It does not talk about a car, a plane, or a train.

title: Grandma's Garden
text: Grandma Rosa grows food behind her house. First, she digs in the ground and takes out each rock. Then she adds seeds and water. She only uses natural things to help the plants, like old leaves. Soon, small green plants come up. Every week, she checks their growth. “Look how tall they are now!” she says to her grandson.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “natural” mean?
options: fake and made in a factory
made by nature, not by people
bought in a can at the store
qs.why: Old leaves come from nature, not from people. A careless reader may think of things from a store, which is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “growth” mean?
qs.why: She says “Look how tall they are now!” so she is checking how much bigger they are getting.

qs.q: What does Grandma Rosa do first?
options: she digs and takes out the rocks
she puts old leaves on the plants
she checks how tall the plants are
qs.why: The passage says “First, she digs in the ground and takes out each rock.” The seeds come after that.

title: The Math Test
text: Mia is a student in the fifth grade. On Friday, she has a math test. All week, she studies at the kitchen table. Some of the problems are difficult, so her big brother helps her. On Monday, the teacher hands back the papers. Her hard work has a good result: 98 out of 100! Nearly every answer is right.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “difficult” mean?
qs.why: Her brother helps her because some problems are hard. “Easy” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “nearly” mean?
options: every single one, with no mistakes
qs.why: She gets 98 out of 100, so almost every answer is right, but not all of them.

qs.q: How did Mia do on the test?
options: she got a perfect score with no mistakes
very well, with only a small mistake
she did badly because she did not study
qs.why: Her hard work gives her 98 out of 100: very good, but not perfect. A careless reader may pick a perfect score.

title: A New Town
text: Leo's family moves to a small town. On the first day, Leo feels alone. He has no friends there. Then he walks down his street and sees some kids playing chess outside a house. A girl named Zara waves. “Do you want to join our chess club?” she asks. Leo is very happy to meet them. Now he goes every Tuesday.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “alone” mean?
options: with no other people; with no friends
qs.why: He has no friends in the new town, so he feels like he has no one with him.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “join” mean?
qs.why: Zara asks if Leo wants to be in their chess club. “Join” can also mean to put two things together, but here it is about a group.

qs.q: How does Leo find new friends?
options: his mother takes him to school
he reads about a club online
Zara comes to his house on the first day
he plays football in the park
he sees kids playing chess on his street
qs.why: He walks down his street, sees kids playing chess, and Zara asks him to join their club.

title: Nora's Birthday
text: It is Nora's birthday. Her dad gives her a present in a blue box. Inside is a book about stars. He also gives her a card. On it, he writes, “To my daughter, with love.” Nora hugs him. “This is perfect!” she says. That night, she reads the book in bed.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “present” mean?
qs.why: Her dad gives it to her for her birthday, so it is a gift. “Present” can also mean now, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “perfect” mean?
qs.why: Nora hugs her dad and loves the book, so for her it is just right.

qs.q: What is inside the blue box?
qs.why: “Inside is a book about stars.” The card is given to her too, but it is not in the box.

title: Rain at the Picnic
text: Jada and her friends have a plan: a picnic in the park. They sit outside on a big blanket. Then dark clouds come, and rain starts. They cover the food with a towel and run quickly to a small café. Inside, they eat their sandwiches by the window and watch the rain.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “cover” mean?
qs.why: They put a towel over the food so the rain does not get it wet.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “quickly” mean?
qs.why: Rain starts, so they run fast to the café. “Slowly” is the opposite.

qs.q: Why do Jada and her friends go to the café?
options: because it is too hot outside
qs.why: Dark clouds come and rain starts, so they run inside. They still eat their sandwiches, so they did not forget the food.

title: At the Bus Station
text: Ravi and his mom are at the bus station early in the morning. Their bus leaves in one hour. Ravi has his bag ready. “Follow me,” Mom says, and they walk to Gate 4. A long line of people is ahead of them. “Will we miss the bus?” Ravi asks. “No,” says Mom. “We have lots of time.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “ahead” mean?
qs.why: The line of people is in front of them, so they must wait. “Behind” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “miss” mean?
options: feel sad because someone is away
not get there in time to get on
qs.why: Ravi is afraid they will not get on the bus in time. “Miss” can also mean feeling sad when someone is away, but not here.

qs.q: Is Mom worried about the bus?
options: yes, she thinks they are late
yes, because Ravi has no bag
no, because the bus has already left
yes, because they are at the wrong gate
no, she thinks they have lots of time
no, because they will take a car
qs.why: Mom says “No” and “We have lots of time.” The bus leaves in one hour.

title: Soup on a Cold Day
text: It is a cold day, so Lucy's dad makes soup. The soup is simple to make. He puts a little oil in a pot, then onions, carrots, and water. After thirty minutes, the soup is done. It is very hot, so Lucy waits a little. Then they eat it with bread and a cup of tea.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “simple” mean?
qs.why: He makes it with only a few things in thirty minutes, so it is easy. “Hard” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “oil” mean?
options: a liquid from plants used in cooking
qs.why: He puts it in the pot to cook the soup. Water is added too, but it is named on its own.

qs.q: Why does Lucy wait before she eats?
options: she is waiting for her tea
qs.why: The passage says “It is very hot, so Lucy waits a little.” The soup is already done.

title: The Lost Key
text: Ahmed comes home from work, but he cannot open the door. His key is missing! He looks in his bag and his coat. “Did I forget it at work?” he thinks. He calls his wife. “Guess where it is,” she says, laughing. “It is on the kitchen table. I am home now. I will let you in.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “missing” mean?
options: not where it should be; lost
qs.why: He cannot find the key in his bag or coat, so it is not where it should be.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “Guess” mean?
options: try to give an answer without knowing for sure
qs.why: His wife wants him to try to say where the key is. He does not know, so he can only guess.

qs.q: Where is Ahmed's key?
options: on the kitchen table at home
qs.why: His wife says “It is on the kitchen table.” He thinks it may be at work, but it is not.

title: A New Song
text: Every morning, Elena listens to the radio while she makes breakfast. Today, she hears a new song. The singer has a soft, warm voice. Elena loves it. Later, she finds out that it is on a new album. It is very popular. All her friends know it too.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “album” mean?
options: a group of songs that come out together
qs.why: The song is part of a group of songs that come out together. “Album” can also be a book of photos, but this is about music.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “popular” mean?
qs.why: All her friends know it too, so many people like it.

qs.q: How does Elena first hear the song?
qs.why: She hears it on the radio while she makes breakfast. She only later learns that her friends know it too.

title: The School Race
text: Today is sports day at school. Five kids line up on the track for a race. Kim is small, but she is very fast. When they start, she runs at top speed. At first, two boys are in front, and Kim is behind. Then, little by little, she gets closer. In the final few steps, she passes them both and wins!

qs.q: In the passage, what does “track” mean?
options: a mark left by a foot
qs.why: The kids line up on it to run the race. “Track” can also be a mark from a foot, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “final” mean?
qs.why: She passes the boys at the end and wins, so it is the last part of the race.

qs.q: How does Kim win the race?
options: she is first from the start
she passes the two boys near the end
qs.why: At first she is behind two boys, and she passes them in the last part. She is not first from the start.

title: A House for Birds
text: Mateo and his grandpa want to build a house for birds. Grandpa has lots of experience. He has worked with wood for forty years. They find an old board in the garage, and Grandpa cuts it into six parts. Mateo holds each part while Grandpa puts in the nails. The house is not huge, but it is just right. The next day, a bird moves in. “Amazing!” says Mateo.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “experience” mean?
options: one thing that happened to you
what you learn from doing something for a long time
qs.why: He has worked with wood for forty years, so he knows a lot from doing it.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “huge” mean?
qs.why: The house is just right for a bird; it is not very, very big.

qs.q: How does Mateo help his grandpa?
options: he holds each part while Grandpa puts in the nails
qs.why: Grandpa cuts the board and puts in the nails; Mateo holds each part.

title: A Message Far Away
text: Sara's brother, Ali, works in a foreign country. He is far away, but they talk every week. Today is his birthday, so Sara sends him a text: “Happy birthday! How are you?” An hour later, she gets his answer: “I am great, thank you! I hope to visit soon.” Sara smiles. His message makes her very happy.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “foreign” mean?
options: of a country that is not their own
qs.why: Ali works in a country that is not Sara and Ali's own country.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “text” mean?
options: a written message sent by phone
qs.why: Sara writes a short message and sends it to Ali's phone. They do not talk with voices this time.

qs.q: Why does Sara send Ali a text today?
qs.why: The passage says “Today is his birthday,” so she writes “Happy birthday!”

title: The Science Fair
text: Our school has a science fair. Kofi and his friend Dani do a project on the sun and the planets. They create a model with balls of paper and paint. A small lamp in the middle is the sun. Many kids say it is very interesting and ask lots of questions. Their table gets a lot of attention all day.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “model” mean?
options: a person who wears clothes for photos
a small thing made to look like a big thing
qs.why: The balls of paper show the sun and planets in a small size. “Model” can also be a person in photos, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “attention” mean?
qs.why: Many kids come, look, and ask questions all day.

qs.q: What is the small lamp for?
options: it shows the sun in the model
qs.why: “A small lamp in the middle is the sun.” The balls of paper are the planets.

title: Mr. Chen at Work
text: Mr. Chen works at a big store in the city. He is in the shoe department. Every day, he helps people find the right size. This month, he gets training on a new computer, so he can find shoes faster. Mr. Chen likes his job a lot. He hopes to work there for his entire career.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “department” mean?
options: a small shop near the store
one part of a big store
qs.why: He works in the part of the store that sells shoes.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “entire” mean?
qs.why: He wants to stay there for all of his working life, the whole of it.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Chen get training this month?
options: because he is new at the store
so he can move to the city
because he does not like his job
so he can find shoes faster on the new computer
qs.why: The passage says he gets training on a new computer “so he can find shoes faster.”

title: Ice on the Lake
text: In winter, the lake by Hana's home turns to ice. Every day, her father checks it. “It is not safe yet,” he says. “It is too thin, and the water below is deep.” Hana waits for two weeks. When he is certain it is thick enough, he says yes. Hana puts on her skates and goes round and round with a big smile.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “certain” mean?
qs.why: He says yes only when he is sure the ice is thick enough.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “deep” mean?
qs.why: The water under the ice goes far down, so falling in would be bad.

qs.q: Why must Hana wait to skate?
options: the ice is too thin at first
qs.why: Her father says the ice is too thin and not safe yet.

title: An Old Picture
text: Grandma Lucia shows me an old picture. In it, a young couple stands in front of a church. “That is me and your grandpa,” she says. “We got married in 1970.” Next, she shows me a photo of a baby. “This is your dad. He was born a year later.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “couple” mean?
options: a few, maybe two or three
two people who are together, like a husband and wife
qs.why: The two people are Grandma and Grandpa, who got married. “A couple” can also mean a few things, but here it is two people together.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “born” mean?
options: came into the world as a baby
qs.why: The baby in the photo is the dad, and he came into the world a year after the wedding.

qs.q: Who is the baby in the photo?
qs.why: Grandma says “This is your dad.”

title: Library Day
text: Every Thursday, Ms. Diaz takes her class to the library. Each child makes a list of books to look for. Lin is learning a new language, Spanish. She finds a book in English and Spanish with a funny title: Cats Do Not Like Hats. On the first page, she knows only one Spanish word: gato. It means cat.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “title” mean?
options: the first word in a book
the person who wrote the book
qs.why: Cats Do Not Like Hats is the name of the book.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “language” mean?
options: the words people use to speak and write
qs.why: Spanish is the new set of words Lin is learning to speak and write.

qs.q: How much Spanish does Lin know?
options: a lot; she reads the whole book easily
she speaks it at home every day
very little; she knows only one word on the first page
she is the best in her class
she teaches it to Ms. Diaz
qs.why: She knows only one Spanish word on the first page, so she knows very little Spanish so far.

title: Under the Stars
text: Tonight, Jamal and his aunt drive far from the city, where the sky is very dark. They lie on a blanket and look up at the night sky. “Each star is a sun, very far from the earth,” his aunt says. For a moment, they are quiet. Then a small light moves across the sky. “Perhaps it is a plane,” says Jamal.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “Perhaps” mean?
qs.why: Jamal is not sure what the light is, so he says maybe.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “dark” mean?
qs.why: Far from the city there are few lights, so the sky has little light. “Bright” is the opposite.

qs.q: Why do Jamal and his aunt drive far from the city?
options: because the city is too cold
to find a dark place to look at the stars
qs.why: They go where the sky is very dark and look up at the night sky. With no city lights, the stars are easier to see. Nothing in the passage is about catching a plane.

title: Apples for Sale
text: Ben and his sister have too many apples from their tree. They put a table on the street in front of their house. They charge one dollar for a bag. A woman offers to buy five bags for her class. By noon, their total is twenty dollars. They share it: ten dollars for Ben and ten for his sister.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “charge” mean?
qs.why: They ask one dollar for each bag. “Charge” can also mean to put power into a phone, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “total” mean?
qs.why: All the money they got by noon, added together, is twenty dollars.

qs.q: How much money does Ben get?
qs.why: They have twenty dollars in all and share it: ten for Ben and ten for his sister.

title: Grandpa Goes Online
text: Grandpa Joe is 80, and he wants to learn about the internet. His granddaughter Aisha helps him. First, she shows him a website with news. He reads an article about baseball. Then she teaches him to make online video calls. “This is easy!” he says. “I am a modern man now!” Now he calls his old friends every Sunday.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “online” mean?
options: on an old phone with a cord
qs.why: He makes video calls on the internet, not face to face.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “modern” mean?
qs.why: Grandpa is joking that he now uses new things from today, like video calls.

qs.q: What does Grandpa do every Sunday now?
options: he reads about baseball at the library
he talks with his old friends by video
qs.why: The last sentence says “Now he calls his old friends every Sunday,” using what Aisha taught him.

title: The Town Council
text: Our town has a council of seven people. Each member lives here. On Tuesday, there is a meeting about one issue: an old empty area near the school. Some people want a dog park. Others want a garden. Everyone gets to talk. Then the seven people vote. The decision is a garden with a small space for dogs. Most people are happy.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “issue” mean?
options: an important problem or subject people talk about
qs.why: The meeting is about one subject people talk about: what to do with the empty area.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “decision” mean?
qs.why: After everyone talks and votes, they choose what to do.

qs.q: What does the council choose?
options: a garden that also has a little space for dogs
qs.why: The decision is “a garden with a small space for dogs,” so it is not a garden only.

title: The Big Parade
text: Every year, our city has a big parade. People stand on both sides of the road to watch. First, a band from the army marches by. They all move their feet at the same time. The sound of the drums is very loud. Then a group of old soldiers walks past. People clap for a long time to show respect.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “marches” mean?
options: walks with the same steps at the same time as others
qs.why: The band members move their feet at the same time as they walk. “March” is also a month, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “respect” mean?
options: thinking someone is good and important, and being kind to them
qs.why: People clap for a long time because they think the old soldiers are important.

qs.q: Who comes first in the parade?
qs.why: “First, a band from the army marches by.” The old soldiers come after that.

title: The School Play
text: Our class is putting on a play, and I get to be the king! Every day after school, we practice our lines. Ms. Okafor is the director. She tells us where to go on the stage. My character is a little silly and loves cake. Our performance is on Friday night. Mom and Dad will sit in the first row.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “practice” mean?
options: do it many times to get better
qs.why: They say their lines every day after school so they can do it well.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “character” mean?
options: what a person is like inside
a letter like A or B
qs.why: The king in the play is the person the writer is playing in the story.

qs.q: When is the show?
qs.why: “Our performance is on Friday night.” They practice every day, but the show is on Friday.

title: A Walk by the River
text: On Saturday, Wei and her uncle go out for the day. They walk to the west next to a river. At first, the path is straight and flat. Then they come to a small bridge and cross to the other side. After two hours, Wei has no energy left. They sit on a big rock, eat some fruit, and soon she feels strong again.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “straight” mean?
options: going in one line, with no turns
qs.why: The path goes in one line at first. “With many turns” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “energy” mean?
qs.why: After two hours of walking, Wei is too tired to keep moving.

qs.q: Why do Wei and her uncle stop at the rock?
options: the path ends at the river
Wei is tired and needs to rest and eat
qs.why: Wei has no energy left, so they sit, eat fruit, and she feels strong again.

title: Omar's New Bike
text: Omar wanted a new bike for his birthday. His old bike was too small for him now. He worked at his uncle's shop every Saturday to save money. After six months, he had enough. He went to the store with his mother to pay for a red bike. Omar felt very happy as he rode it home.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “pay” mean?
options: to ask for it as a gift
to look at it for a long time
to give money to get it
qs.why: Omar saved money for six months and then gave it to the store for the bike. He did not get it as a gift.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “new” mean?
options: bought a short time ago; not old
qs.why: Omar wanted a bike that was not old, because his old bike was too small.

qs.q: Why did Omar work at his uncle's shop?
options: To save money for a new bike
To learn how to fix bikes
Because his mother told him to
To buy a gift for his mother
Because his old bike was broken
qs.why: He worked every Saturday to save money, and then he paid for a bike. His old bike was too small, not broken.

title: Rain at the Game
text: Our soccer team played the Blue Hawks on Sunday. In the morning, it started to rain. We played anyway. The ball was hard to control on the wet grass. At the end, the Blue Hawks won by one goal. Coach Park said, 'You all played hard. Keep trying!' We still had fun.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “trying” mean?
options: working hard to do something well
tasting something to see if you like it
qs.why: The coach wants the players to keep working hard to play well. Here it does not mean tasting food, and it is the opposite of giving up.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “control” mean?
options: to make it go where you want
to find it after losing it
qs.why: On wet grass the ball was hard to make go where the players wanted.

qs.q: Did the writer's team win the game?
options: No, they lost by one goal, but they still had fun
Yes, they won by one goal
No, the game was stopped by the rain
Yes, and the coach said they were the best
No, and they were very sad
No one won; the score was the same
qs.why: The Blue Hawks won by one goal, so the writer's team lost. But the writer says 'We still had fun.'

title: Sundays with Grandma
text: Every Sunday, Lucia helps her grandma cook. They make soup with beans and rice. Grandma always tells stories about her life in a little town by the sea. Lucia loves these stories. When the soup is ready, the whole family sits at the table and eats together.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “life” mean?
options: the time she lived there, and what she did then
qs.why: Grandma tells stories about the years she lived in the town. It is not just her house.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “whole” mean?
options: all of it, with no one left out
qs.why: The whole family means everyone in the family. “Hole” sounds the same but is a different word.

qs.q: What does Lucia do every Sunday?
options: She visits a little town by the sea
She cooks alone for her family
She buys beans and rice at a store
She cooks soup with her grandma and hears her stories
She goes to the sea with her family
qs.why: Lucia helps her grandma make soup, and Grandma tells the stories, not Lucia.

title: A Trip to the City
text: Last week, Mei and her dad took a train to the city. They rode for almost three hours. Then they went to the top of a tall tower. From up there, Mei could see for miles. The cars below looked like toys. She took many pictures on her phone.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “top” mean?
qs.why: They went to the highest part of the tower, so the cars below looked small.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “almost” mean?
qs.why: The ride was nearly three hours, a little less than three.

qs.q: Why did the cars look like toys?
options: Mei saw them from the train
Mei was looking at them from high up
qs.why: From the top of the tall tower the real cars below looked small, like toys.

title: The Lost Dog
text: One night, Sam heard a dog crying outside. It was a small brown dog, and it was lost. Sam gave it water and let it sleep in the kitchen. In the morning, he put a picture of the dog online. Soon, a woman called him. 'That's my dog!' she said. She was so thankful.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “lost” mean?
options: not able to find its way home
qs.why: The dog could not find its way home, and later its owner called.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “let” mean?
qs.why: Sam allowed the dog to sleep in his kitchen.

qs.q: How did the woman find her dog?
options: She heard the dog crying at night
She saw signs on the street
She saw the picture Sam put online
qs.why: Sam put a picture online, and then the woman called him. Sam did not call her first.

title: Moving Day
text: Today the Okafor family is moving to a new house. Dad carries big boxes to the truck. Mom puts her guitar in its case so it will not break. Little Ada holds her cat. She feels a bit sad to leave her old room. But her new room has a big window that looks out on a park.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “case” mean?
options: a box or cover that keeps things safe
qs.why: Mom puts her guitar in its case so it will not break, so the case keeps it safe.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “bit” mean?
qs.why: Ada is a little sad, but the next sentence says her new room is nice.

qs.q: Why does Ada feel sad?
options: Her new room is very small
She cannot go to the park
She has to leave her old room
She does not like the truck
qs.why: The passage says she feels sad to leave her old room. Her new room has a big window, so it is not small.

title: The Science Fair
text: Jamal's class has a science fair next Friday. He wants to learn which drink helps plants grow best. He put three plants by the window. He gave each one a different drink: water, milk, and juice. Every day he checks them and writes notes. He thinks the plant with water will do best. At the fair, he will show his chart.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “different” mean?
options: not the same as the others
qs.why: Each plant got a drink that was not the same: water, milk, or juice.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “checks” mean?
options: looks at them to see how they are doing
moves them to a new place
qs.why: Every day Jamal looks at the plants to see if they are growing, then writes notes.

qs.q: What is Jamal trying to find out?
options: Which drink makes a plant grow best
How much water a plant can hold
Which window gets the most sun
qs.why: He gave each plant a different drink to learn which drink helps plants grow best.

title: The Bus Driver
text: Mr. Diaz drives a bus. His job has an early start, at five in the morning. He knows many riders by name. He says hello to each person who gets on. When an old man needs help with his bags, Mr. Diaz waits for him. People in the area like him a lot.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “area” mean?
qs.why: People in the area are the people who live in that part of town.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “waits” mean?
options: stays until the man is ready
qs.why: Mr. Diaz does not drive away. He stays until the old man is on the bus.

qs.q: What kind of person is Mr. Diaz?
options: Friendly and patient with his riders
qs.why: He knows riders by name, says hello to each one, and waits for an old man. He starts at five, so he is not late.

title: Music Night
text: On Friday, the school had a music night. Students sang songs and played drums. Priya played the piano. She was scared at first, but her friend smiled at her from the front row. The room was full of parents who came to watch. When it was over, everyone clapped. Priya felt great.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “full” mean?
qs.why: So many parents came that there was no empty space in the room.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “great” mean?
qs.why: After everyone clapped, Priya felt very good. She was scared only at first.

qs.q: What helped Priya when she was scared?
qs.why: The passage says she was scared at first, but her friend smiled at her from the front row.

title: At the Doctor
text: Ben did not feel well, so his mom took him to the doctor. 'Where does it hurt?' asked Dr. Silva. 'My head and my back,' said Ben. The doctor looked in his ears and his mouth. 'You have a cold,' she said. 'Drink lots of water and rest. Your health is important.'

qs.q: In the passage, what does “back” mean?
options: the part of your arm that bends
the part of the body behind you
qs.why: Ben is telling the doctor where he hurts, so it is a part of his body, the part behind him.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “health” mean?
options: how well or sick your body is
qs.why: The doctor means Ben's body: being well and not sick matters.

qs.q: What does the doctor say is wrong with Ben?
options: He has a problem with his ears
qs.why: Dr. Silva says, 'You have a cold.' She looked in his ears, but she did not say his ears were the problem.

title: Kenji's Plan
text: Kenji wants to buy a board game. It costs forty dollars, but he has only twenty. His sister has an idea. 'People on our street need someone to wash their cars,' she says. Kenji is not sure it will work, but he makes a sign. Five neighbors pay him. Soon he has forty dollars.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “sure” mean?
qs.why: Kenji is 'not sure,' so he has some doubt that the plan will work.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “idea” mean?
options: a plan that came into her mind
qs.why: His sister thought of a plan: wash cars for the neighbors.

qs.q: How did Kenji get the rest of the money?
options: His sister gave it to him
He found it on the street
He washed cars for his neighbors
He made signs for his neighbors
His parents gave it to him
qs.why: His sister's plan was to wash cars, and five neighbors paid him. The sign was only to tell people.

title: Snow Day
text: Winter is Ana's favorite season. Last night, it snowed a lot. Now everything outside is white. There is no school today, so Ana and her brother run out to play. They make a snowman together. It has a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. Their cheeks get pink in the cold air.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “together” mean?
qs.why: Ana and her brother make one snowman with each other.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “season” mean?
options: one of the four parts of the year
qs.why: Winter is one of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, fall, and winter.

qs.q: Why is there probably no school today?
options: It snowed a lot last night
qs.why: The passage says it snowed a lot and everything is white. It is winter, not summer.

title: Ming's Library
text: Ming loves to read. Every Saturday, she goes to the public library near her home. It is free for everyone. Today she got a book about space. It has pictures of stars and planets. She has to bring it back in two weeks. She will finish it in one.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “public” mean?
qs.why: A public library is for all people. The next sentence says it is free for everyone.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “free” mean?
qs.why: Everyone can use the library without paying. “Not busy” is a different meaning of free.

qs.q: How long will it take Ming to read the book?
qs.why: She has two weeks to bring it back, but 'She will finish it in one' means in one week.

title: The Bake Sale
text: Our community center needs a new roof, so we had a bake sale. We made a sign with information about the roof. Mrs. Haddad baked her lemon cake. Kids sold cookies at a table by the door. Many people came, even though it rained. That day we got five hundred dollars! The president of the center thanked us all.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “information” mean?
qs.why: The sign gave facts about the roof, so people knew why the sale was happening.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “president” mean?
options: the person who bakes the cakes
qs.why: Here it is the leader of the community center, not of a country.

qs.q: Why did they have the bake sale?
options: To get money for a new roof
To have fun in the rain
qs.why: The first sentence says the center needs a new roof, 'so we had a bake sale.'

title: Calling Grandpa
text: Carlos lives in Texas. His grandparents are far away in Mexico. Every Sunday, he calls them on the phone. He tells them about school and his soccer games. His grandpa always asks, 'Are you eating well?' Carlos laughs and says, 'Yes, Grandpa!' He hopes to visit them next summer.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “far” mean?
qs.why: His grandparents live a long way from him, in another country.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “well” mean?
qs.why: Grandpa wants to know if Carlos eats good food. A well can also be a hole for water, but not here.

qs.q: How does Carlos talk with his grandparents?
options: They live with him in Texas
He sees them at his soccer games
He calls them on the phone every Sunday
He sends them videos every day
qs.why: He calls them every Sunday. He only hopes to visit next summer.

title: First Day at Work
text: Today is Aisha's first day at her new job. She works in a big office in the middle of town. Her boss, Mr. Lee, shows her to her desk. He gives her a list of things to do. Aisha has many questions, and Mr. Lee answers each one. At lunch, a coworker named Tom asks her to eat with him.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “office” mean?
options: a building or room where people do their jobs
qs.why: Aisha works there and has a desk, so it is a place where people do their jobs.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “things” mean?
qs.why: A list of things to do is a list of jobs or tasks.

qs.q: Who answers Aisha's questions?
qs.why: The passage says Mr. Lee answers each one. Tom only asks her to lunch.

title: Fire Practice
text: At ten o'clock, a loud bell rang at school. It was not a real fire. It was practice. Some kids put their hands over their ears. Ms. Chen said, 'Please stand up and walk to the door.' The children went outside quietly. They stood on the grass and stayed there. After five minutes, Ms. Chen counted them. Everyone was there. 'Good job,' she said.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “please” mean?
options: a word you add to ask nicely
a word to say thank you
a word to show you are angry
qs.why: Ms. Chen adds it to ask the children nicely to stand up.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “stayed” mean?
qs.why: The children stood on the grass and did not leave until Ms. Chen counted them.

qs.q: Why did Ms. Chen count the children?
options: To see who was the fastest
To find out who rang the bell
To make sure everyone was there
qs.why: After she counted, the passage says 'Everyone was there,' so she was checking that no one was missing.

title: Lena's Race
text: Lena wants to win the big race in June. She trains every day after school. Her coach believes she is fast enough. She eats healthy food and gets lots of sleep. On race day, she starts slowly. Near the end, she passes everyone. She comes in first! Her heart is beating fast. Her little brother jumps high with joy.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “believes” mean?
qs.why: Her coach thinks it is true that Lena is fast enough.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “high” mean?
qs.why: Her brother jumps far up off the ground because he is so happy.

qs.q: How did Lena run the race?
options: She was first from start to end
She started fast and got tired
She started slowly and passed everyone near the end
qs.why: She starts slowly, then near the end she passes everyone and comes in first.

title: Lunch at a Café
text: Rosa and Kim met for lunch at a pretty café. It had one small room with flowers on every table. The waiter was kind and helpful. Rosa ordered a cheese sandwich. Kim wanted soup, but it was all gone, so she had a salad. When the bill came, Kim said, 'Let me pay this time.' Rosa smiled and said, 'Thank you!'

qs.q: In the passage, what does “ordered” mean?
options: asked for food she would pay for
put things in a neat line
qs.why: At a café, Rosa asks the waiter for a sandwich. She is not telling anyone what to do.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “pretty” mean?
qs.why: The café has flowers on every table, so it is nice to look at.

qs.q: Why did Kim have a salad?
options: The waiter gave her the wrong food
qs.why: Kim wanted soup, 'but it was all gone,' so she had a salad.

title: The Garden
text: Behind our building, there was an empty piece of land covered in trash. A group of neighbors wanted to change it. First, they cleaned it up. Then each family took a part of the land. They used big buckets to carry water. Old Mr. Novak taught the kids how to plant seeds. Now it is the greenest place on our street.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “part” mean?
qs.why: Each family took one piece of the land, not all of it.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “change” mean?
qs.why: The neighbors made the land different: it went from trash to a green garden.

qs.q: What did the neighbors do first?
options: They gave each family a part
qs.why: The passage says 'First, they cleaned it up.' The other jobs came after.

title: The Museum Trip
text: Mr. Ito's class went to a history museum. They saw coins, maps, and clothes from the past. A guide told them a story about a ship. It sailed across the sea two hundred years ago with a family on it. The children asked many questions. Back at school, each student wrote a short report about one thing they learned.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “report” mean?
options: a piece of writing that gives facts
qs.why: Each student wrote about one thing they learned, so it gives facts.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “ago” mean?
qs.why: The ship sailed two hundred years before now.

qs.q: What was the guide's story about?
options: A ship that crossed the sea long ago
A family that lives by the sea today
A ship that will sail next year
qs.why: The guide told a story about a ship that sailed across the sea two hundred years ago.

title: The Broken Car
text: The Patel family was driving to the beach. Suddenly, the car made a strange noise and stopped. Dad got out and looked at the car. 'I don't know what is wrong,' he said. Mom called a man who fixes cars. He came in his truck one hour later. He fixed the problem fast. His service cost fifty dollars. Soon they were on the road again.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “service” mean?
options: a set of plates for dinner
the work the man did for them
qs.why: The man fixed the car, and that work cost fifty dollars. It was not free.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “wrong” mean?
options: not the way it should be
qs.why: The car stopped, so something in it was not the way it should be.

qs.q: Who fixed the car?
qs.why: Dad did not know what was wrong. Mom called a man who fixes cars, and he fixed the problem.

title: Learning to Swim
text: At age seven, Yuki was afraid of water. Her mom found a swimming course at the pool. The teacher, Ms. Ruiz, was really calm. In the first class, Yuki only put her face in the pool. By the last class, she was able to swim from one side to the other. She was so proud!

qs.q: In the passage, what does “course” mean?
options: a set of classes about one thing
qs.why: It has a first class and a last class, so it is a set of swimming classes.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “last” mean?
options: coming at the end, after all the others
qs.why: The last class is the final one, after all the other classes.

qs.q: How did Yuki change?
options: She stopped going to the pool
She learned to swim in one day
Her mom taught her to swim
She went from being afraid of water to swimming across the pool
qs.why: At first she was afraid, but by the last class she could swim from one side to the other. Ms. Ruiz taught her, not her mom.

title: A New Park Law
text: The city government wants to make a new law. Dogs in the park must walk next to their owners. This rule matters a lot to dog owners. Some like the idea, and some do not. So next Tuesday there will be a meeting at City Hall. Anyone can come and talk about it. Officer Grant from the police will answer questions. The doors will be open at six o'clock.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “matters” mean?
options: is a thing you can touch
qs.why: The rule is important to dog owners because it changes how they walk their dogs.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “open” mean?
options: not closed, so people can go in
qs.why: At six o'clock the doors will not be closed, so people can go in to the meeting. 'Locked' is the opposite.

qs.q: Why will there be a meeting?
options: To pick a new police officer
To say the law is already done
So people can talk about the new dog law
qs.why: Some people like the idea and some do not, so there is a meeting where anyone can talk about it.

title: Under the Stars
text: Last summer, Diego and his uncle went camping in the north of the state. They set their bags down by a lake and put up a tent. At night, the sky was black, and there were so many stars. Their light was soft and bright. The city felt far away. Diego made a wish and fell asleep.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “state” mean?
options: one of the large parts of a country like the US
qs.why: They went to the north part of one state, a large part of a country.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “set” mean?
qs.why: They put their bags down by the lake before they put up the tent.

qs.q: Where did Diego and his uncle put up their tent?
options: In the south of the state
qs.why: The passage says they set their bags down by a lake and put up a tent. They were in the north, not the south.

title: Grandpa's Photos
text: Grandpa Femi has a box of photos. One rainy afternoon, he looks at them with his granddaughter, Zara. 'This is me when I was young,' he says. 'And this girl is your grandma. We met at a birthday party.' He smiles. 'I remember the music and the cake. It was a special day.' Zara asks him to tell her more.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “party” mean?
options: a group that wants to run the government
a time when people meet to eat and have fun
qs.why: A birthday party has music and cake, so it is a time for fun. It is not a political party here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “remember” mean?
options: still has it in his mind; does not forget
qs.why: Many years later, Grandpa still has the music and the cake in his mind. He did not forget them.

qs.q: Where did Grandpa meet Grandma?
qs.why: Grandpa says, 'We met at a birthday party.' The rainy afternoon is when he shows Zara the photos.

title: Soup in Winter
text: Hana has her own ice cream shop. In summer, her business is very good. But in winter, the shop is often empty because people do not want cold food. So Hana began to sell hot soup. Now many local workers come in for lunch. A large bowl costs six dollars. In winter, half of her money now comes from soup.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “own” mean?
qs.why: The shop is Hana's and not someone else's.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “local” mean?
options: from the area near the shop
qs.why: The workers who come for lunch work in the area near the shop.

qs.q: Why did Hana start selling soup?
options: Ice cream is bad for you
She closed the shop in summer
Few people want ice cream in winter
qs.why: In winter the shop was often empty because people do not want cold food, so she sold hot soup.

title: Storm Coming
text: Every morning, Tariq and his dad eat breakfast with the TV on. Today, a man on the news says a big storm is coming from the south. It will probably reach their town by noon. Tariq looks outside. Dark clouds hang low in the sky. His dad gives him his rain boots. 'Maybe you will need these,' he says.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “probably” mean?
qs.why: The man thinks the storm will very likely come by noon, but he cannot be fully sure.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “low” mean?
options: close to the ground; not high
qs.why: The clouds are near the ground, not high up in the sky.

qs.q: Why does Dad give Tariq his rain boots?
options: Tariq's old boots are too small
The man on TV said to wear boots
A storm is on the way
qs.why: The news says a big storm will probably come by noon, and dark clouds are outside. It is not raining yet.

title: Counting Bees
text: Dr. Amara Bello teaches at a university. She and her students do research on bees. Each day, they count how many bees visit the flowers in a field. They put all the data on a computer. Their work helps farmers understand which flowers bees like best. Dr. Bello says bees are very important for our food.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “research” mean?
options: careful study to find new facts
qs.why: Dr. Bello and her students study bees to learn new facts about them.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “data” mean?
qs.why: The data is the numbers they count each day, like how many bees visit.

qs.q: Why does the team count bees?
options: To learn how to use a computer
To help farmers know which flowers bees like
qs.why: Their work helps farmers understand which flowers bees like best.

title: A New Friend
text: Last year, Nadia's family moved to a new country. At first, school was hard for her. She did not speak any English, and she was sure she would never make friends. But a girl named Lily sat with her at lunch, and she did not miss a single day. Now Nadia speaks English well, and Lily is her best friend.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “hard” mean?
qs.why: School was not easy because Nadia did not speak English. “Not soft” is another meaning of hard.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “never” mean?
qs.why: Nadia thought there would be no time at all when she would make friends.

qs.q: How did Lily help Nadia?
options: She sat with her at lunch every day
qs.why: Lily sat with Nadia at lunch and did not miss a single day.

title: The Corner Bakery
text: When Amara opened a small bakery on Pine Street, she had a tight budget. She could not buy new ovens, so she used two old ones from her aunt. Every morning she baked fresh bread before the sun came up. At first, few people came in. Then a teacher from the school across the street began to purchase a loaf every day. She started to recommend the bakery to the parents at her school. Slowly the line at the door grew longer. For the first six months, Amara made no profit at all, because flour and rent cost so much. Eventually, after almost a year, she earned enough to pay herself a small wage and hire a helper.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “budget” mean?
options: a large amount of money saved in a bank
a plan for how much money she could spend
a loan she had to pay back
a list of the breads she would bake
qs.why: A budget is a plan for spending money; a “tight” budget means she had little to spend. “Cheap” is a different use of budget as an adjective, not the meaning here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “Eventually” mean?
options: at a later time, after a long wait
qs.why: Eventually means at some later time after a long wait; here it came “after almost a year.” It does not mean “perhaps.”

qs.q: Why did Amara make no profit in the first six months?
options: Nobody ever came into the bakery
She gave all her bread away for free
Her costs for flour and rent were high
She paid a helper too much
qs.why: The passage says she made no profit “because flour and rent cost so much.” She hired a helper only later, after almost a year.

title: A Lost Wallet
text: On his way home from work, Tomás noticed a brown wallet lying on the bus seat next to him. Inside were some cash, a bank card, and a library card with a name: Grace Okafor. Tomás is an honest man, so he never thought about keeping the money. He found Grace online and contacted her with a short message. She wrote back within an hour. Apparently, she had been looking for the wallet all afternoon and had called the bus company twice. When they met at a café the next day, she said she felt great relief. A week later, Tomás received a thank-you card and a box of cookies in the mail.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “Apparently” mean?
options: clearly, so that anyone could see it
based on what she told him, though he could not be sure
qs.why: Apparently means “from what he heard,” here from Grace’s message. It does not mean “clearly” or “without doubt.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “relief” mean?
options: help such as food or money given to people in need
anger that someone took her wallet
a good feeling that her worry was over
qs.why: Relief is the good feeling when worry ends; she had been worried about her wallet. Help given to people in need is a different meaning of relief.

qs.q: How did Tomás find the owner of the wallet?
options: He gave the wallet to the bus driver
She called him after seeing his number
He used the name on a card inside it to look for her online
He took the wallet to the library
He waited at the bus stop for her
qs.why: He saw the name Grace Okafor on the library card and “found Grace online.” It was Grace, not Tomás, who called the bus company.

title: The Science Fair
text: For the school science fair, Priya wanted to conduct a test on the water in three ponds near her town. She took a small sample from each pond in a clean glass jar. At home, she used a simple kit to measure how much dirt was in the water. Her method was to test each jar three times and then use the middle number. Her teacher said this made the results more accurate, because one bad test would not change the answer. Priya was determined to finish before the fair, so she worked on her poster every evening for two weeks. In the end, she found that the pond near the farm was the dirtiest.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “sample” mean?
options: a free gift from a shop
all of the water in the pond
a small amount that shows what the whole pond is like
a short piece of a song used in another song
qs.why: A sample is a small amount that shows what the whole is like. She took a little water from each pond, not all of it.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “determined” mean?
options: found out the facts about something
told what to do by her teacher
firmly decided not to let anything stop her
qs.why: Determined (adjective) means having a firm decision and not letting anything stop you. “Found out the facts” is a meaning of the verb determine, not this word here.

qs.q: Why did testing each jar three times help Priya?
options: One bad test would not change her final answer much
It was faster than testing once
Her teacher did the tests for her
It let her test more ponds
qs.why: The teacher said three tests made the results more accurate “because one bad test would not change the answer.”

title: Grandpa's Garden
text: Every spring, Lena helps her grandfather plant his garden. He only grows plants that are native to their part of the country, because they have lived there for thousands of years and need little extra water. “Bees and butterflies know these plants,” he says. Last year they found twelve species of butterfly in the garden, including one that is rare in their area. To protect the young plants from rabbits, Lena puts a low fence around them. Her grandfather typically waters early in the morning, before the day gets hot. Lena thinks he is very wise. He says he simply learned from his own mistakes over fifty years.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “native” mean?
options: growing in that place from the beginning, not brought from far away
qs.why: Native plants belong to a place from its beginning; that is why “they have lived there for thousands of years.” “Brought from another country” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “typically” mean?
qs.why: Typically means in the usual way, in most cases. The passage describes his normal habit of watering in the morning.

qs.q: Why does Lena's grandfather grow only native plants?
options: They are cheaper at the store
Lena asked him to grow them
They grow faster than other plants
They suit the area and need little extra water
qs.why: He grows them because they have lived there a long time and “need little extra water.” Rabbits do eat them, which is why Lena builds a fence.

title: The Job Interview
text: Last month, Kwame decided to apply for a job as a manager at a sports store. He was one of eight candidates, and some of them had more experience than he did. To prepare, he read about the company and practiced answers with his sister. In the interview, they asked about his background. He explained that he grew up helping in his father's shop and later studied business at night. He spoke with confidence, and he was also frank: he said he had never led a team before, but he was ready to learn. Two days later, the company called to offer him the job. They liked that he told the truth.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “candidates” mean?
options: workers who already had jobs at the store
people trying to be chosen for the job
people trying to win an election
qs.why: Here candidates are the eight people competing for the manager job. The word can also be used for elections, but there is no election in this story.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “frank” mean?
options: honest and direct, even about something not nice to hear
qs.why: Being frank means saying the truth directly. Kwame openly said he had never led a team, which did not make him look good.

qs.q: What does the passage suggest was a main reason Kwame got the job?
options: He had more experience than everyone else
His father owned the sports store
He had led many teams before
The company liked his honesty about what he had not done
His sister worked at the company
He was the only person who applied
qs.why: The last line says “They liked that he told the truth.” Other candidates had more experience, so that was not the reason.

title: Saving for a Bike
text: Mia, who is eleven, wanted a new bike. The one she liked in the shop window was expensive: it cost three hundred dollars. She could not afford it with the forty dollars in her money box. Her mother gave her two options. She could buy a cheap bike now, or she could wait and save. Mia chose to save. She walked the neighbors' dogs regularly, every Tuesday and Saturday, and earned ten dollars each time. After four months, she counted her money and had enough. “It feels better because I paid for it myself,” she said, as she rode the new bike to school.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “afford” mean?
options: have enough money to pay for
qs.why: To afford something is to have enough money to pay for it. Forty dollars was not enough for a 300-dollar bike.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “regularly” mean?
options: again and again at the same times
only when she felt like it
qs.why: Regularly means happening again and again at the same times; she walked the dogs every Tuesday and Saturday.

qs.q: How did Mia get enough money for the bike?
options: Her mother paid for half of it
She walked dogs for neighbors twice a week
She found extra money in her money box
She bought a cheap bike instead
qs.why: She earned ten dollars each time she walked the dogs, every Tuesday and Saturday, for four months.

title: A Wall Across England
text: Hadrian's Wall is an ancient stone wall in the north of England. The Roman Empire began building it around the year 122, when Hadrian was the emperor. It ran for approximately 73 miles, from one coast of the island to the other. Most of the construction took about six years, and soldiers did much of the work. The wall marked the northern edge of Roman territory, and it helped soldiers watch who came and went. Small forts were built along it, where soldiers lived. Today, long parts of the wall remain, and many people walk beside it on a path through the hills.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “territory” mean?
options: an area that one wild animal guards
qs.why: Territory is land controlled by a country or group. Here it means the land the Romans ruled; the wall marked its northern edge.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “approximately” mean?
qs.why: Approximately means close to a number but not exactly. The wall was about 73 miles long.

qs.q: According to the passage, what was one use of the wall when it was built?
options: To give visitors a path for walking
To keep the sea from flooding the land
To carry water across the country
To show where two coasts met
To help soldiers watch who came and went
To hold up a road through the hills
qs.why: The passage says it marked the edge of Roman land and “helped soldiers watch who came and went.” The walking path is for visitors today, not its first use.

title: The Night Shift
text: Nurse Elena Petrova works the night shift in a busy hospital. Just after midnight, a young man arrived after falling off his bike. It was an emergency: his arm was badly hurt and he was losing blood. Elena immediately called the doctor and stopped the bleeding. The injury was serious, but his life was not in danger. Her next task was simpler: she helped an older woman find her glasses and get back to sleep. By morning, Elena was tired, but she stayed after her shift to talk with the young man's mother. “His recovery will take about two months,” she explained. Her co-workers say she is the most dedicated nurse on the floor.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “recovery” mean?
options: the cost of his hospital stay
the process of getting well again
getting back something that was lost
the trip home from the hospital
qs.why: Recovery here is the process of getting well after being hurt. Getting back a lost thing is a different meaning that does not fit.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “dedicated” mean?
options: given to someone as an honor, like a book
giving a lot of time and effort because she cares
qs.why: A dedicated nurse gives a lot of time and effort because she cares, like staying after her shift. A book can be dedicated to someone, but that meaning does not fit a person here.

qs.q: Why did Elena stay at the hospital after her shift?
options: To help an older woman find her glasses
To talk with the young man's mother
Because the young man's life was in danger
qs.why: The passage says she “stayed after her shift to talk with the young man's mother.” She helped the older woman during the night, before morning.

title: The Robot Vacuum
text: When the Nguyen family bought a robot vacuum, the children thought it was magic. Mr. Nguyen used his phone to schedule cleaning for ten o'clock every morning, when everyone was out. At ten, the machine started automatically and moved around the rooms on its own. It could clean wood floors and carpets, and it changed its power for each surface. Once a month, the phone told them to update the robot's software. It also needed some simple maintenance: someone had to empty the dust box and clean the brushes. Obviously, it could not climb stairs, so the family carried it upstairs on Saturdays.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “schedule” mean?
options: plan for it to happen at a set time
qs.why: To schedule is to plan for something to happen at a certain time; he set cleaning for ten o'clock each morning.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “surface” mean?
options: to come up to the top of water
the top layer, such as a floor or carpet
qs.why: Surface here is the top layer the robot cleans, like a wood floor or carpet. “To come up to the top of water” is a verb meaning that does not fit.

qs.q: Why did the family carry the robot upstairs on Saturdays?
options: It needed a software update upstairs
It could not climb stairs by itself
The children wanted to play with it
The phone told them to move it
qs.why: The passage says it “could not climb stairs, so the family carried it upstairs.”

title: A Town Survey
text: Last spring, a small town wanted to know how to use an empty lot near the train station. The town office sent a short survey to every home, with five questions. More than two thousand people answered. A clear majority, about sixty percent, said they would prefer a park to a parking lot. Many people also wrote their own suggestions. One child asked for a place to ride skateboards, and an older man wanted benches in the shade. The people who wanted parking were mainly those who drove to the station every day. The overall result was clear: most of the town wanted green space.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “majority” mean?
options: more than half of the people
the people who drove to the station
qs.why: A majority is more than half; here about sixty percent of the people who answered.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “mainly” mean?
qs.why: Mainly means mostly. Most of the people who wanted parking drove to the station, but not necessarily every one of them.

qs.q: What did the survey show most people wanted?
options: A park on the empty lot
qs.why: About sixty percent preferred a park, and overall “most of the town wanted green space.” The skateboard place and benches were single people’s ideas.

title: A Lake in the Mountains
text: Every summer, Diego and his uncle make the long journey north to a quiet lake in the mountains. It takes two days by car. This year, his uncle showed him how to check the depth of the water with a rope and a small weight. “Big fish like the cold water near the bottom,” he said. On the first morning, Diego only caught a tiny fish, no longer than his finger, so he put it back. Later, they saw a wild moose drinking at the edge of the lake. On the last day, Diego struggled for ten minutes to pull in a large trout. He was very proud when it finally came out of the water.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “depth” mean?
options: how wide it was from side to side
how many fish were in it
how deep it was from the top to the bottom
qs.why: Depth is how deep something is from the surface to the bottom. His uncle used a rope with a weight to find it. Width is a different measure.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “struggled” mean?
options: tried very hard to do something difficult
qs.why: Struggled means tried very hard at something difficult. He did not fail: the trout “finally came out of the water.”

qs.q: Why did Diego's uncle check how deep the water was?
options: He wanted to swim in the lake
He was looking for the moose
Big fish stay in the cold water near the bottom
He wanted to catch tiny fish
The lake was dangerous for the boat
qs.why: He said, “Big fish like the cold water near the bottom,” so knowing the depth helped them fish.

title: New Rules at the Pool
text: The city pool opened for the summer with a few new rules. For safety, glass bottles are now banned anywhere near the water, because broken glass is hard to see and can cut bare feet. The pool also requires children under ten to have an adult with them at all times. Two lifeguards guard the pool from tall chairs, and they change places every hour so they stay awake and careful. Swimmers need permission from a lifeguard before they use the high diving board. The minimum age for the diving board is twelve. Most families say the rules make the pool a calmer place.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “banned” mean?
qs.why: Banned means officially not allowed. Glass bottles cannot be brought near the water.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “minimum” mean?
options: the lowest age that is allowed
the highest age that is allowed
the best age to learn diving
the age when children start swimming
qs.why: Minimum means the smallest amount allowed, so swimmers must be at least twelve. “Highest age” is the opposite.

qs.q: Why do the lifeguards change places every hour?
options: So each one gets paid more
So they stay awake and careful
To give children permission to dive
Because the pool closes every hour
qs.why: The passage says they change places “so they stay awake and careful.”

title: Two Brothers, Two Lives
text: Sam and Theo are twins, but they live very different lives. Sam lives in a rural area, on a farm with cows and an old red barn. The nearest store is twenty minutes away by car. Theo chose the opposite kind of life. He lives in an urban area, in an apartment on the tenth floor, and he can walk to work, shops, and three movie theaters. The brothers live five hundred miles apart, but they talk on the phone every Sunday. Sam generally gets up at five to feed the animals, while Theo sleeps until seven. Each brother says he is more comfortable where he is, and each one thinks the other is a little silly.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “rural” mean?
options: in the middle of a big city
far from cities, with farms and fields
qs.why: Rural describes places far from cities, like Sam’s farm with cows. “In a big city” describes Theo’s urban life, the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “apart” mean?
qs.why: Apart means separated by distance; the brothers live five hundred miles from each other.

qs.q: Which statement about the brothers is true?
options: Theo wakes up earlier than Sam
Each one wants to move to the other's home
They have not spoken in years
They stay in touch even though they live far away
They live in the same building
qs.why: They live five hundred miles apart but “talk on the phone every Sunday.” Sam, not Theo, gets up earlier.

title: Piano at Forty
text: When Hana Sato started piano lessons at age forty, she worried that she had no talent for music. Her teacher told her that effort matters more than a natural gift. Hana practiced for twenty minutes every evening after dinner. At first, her fingers felt slow and heavy, and she frequently pressed the wrong keys. Her progress was slow, but she could hear it. After six months, she could play a simple song all the way through. She did not play it perfectly, and she still made two small mistakes, but her family clapped. Hana's goal now is to master one piece by Bach before her next birthday.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “talent” mean?
options: a natural ability to do something well
qs.why: Talent is a natural ability. Her teacher contrasts it with effort, calling talent “a natural gift.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “master” mean?
options: learn so well that she can play it easily
qs.why: To master a skill is to learn it so well you can do it easily. “A teacher of music” is a noun meaning that does not fit “to master one piece.”

qs.q: What does the passage suggest about how Hana learned?
options: She learned fast because of her natural gift
She stopped practicing after six months
Her family did not like her playing
Steady practice helped her improve even without natural talent
She can already play Bach perfectly
qs.why: She practiced every evening and made slow but real progress, showing her teacher’s point that effort matters more than talent.

title: After the Storm
text: Last October, a severe storm hit a small town on the coast. Strong winds damaged the roofs of many houses, and one old wooden boathouse was completely destroyed. Some families had no electricity for three days. People from nearby towns drove in with trucks to help. A church group supplied hot meals twice a day, and a local store gave away water and batteries. The government also sent aid, including blankets and money to help families fix their homes. “I have never seen people work together like this,” said Rosa Díaz, who has lived in the town for forty years.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “destroyed” mean?
options: damaged so badly that it could not be fixed
qs.why: Destroyed means damaged so badly it cannot be used or fixed. The word “completely” shows it was worse than the roofs that were only damaged.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “aid” mean?
options: a person who helps a leader
help such as blankets, food, or money
qs.why: Aid is help given to people in need; here the city sent blankets and money.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Most families left the town after the storm
Many people and groups helped the town after the storm
The storm did very little harm
The town had no electricity for a month
qs.why: The passage lists help from nearby towns, a church group, a store, and the city, and Rosa says she has never seen people work together like this.

title: The Reading Club
text: Once a month, a group of eight neighbors attends a reading club at the public library. They read classic works of literature, such as books by Jane Austen and Chinua Achebe, that people still love many years after they were written. Each person reads the book at home. Then they meet on a Thursday evening to discuss it over tea. Not everyone has the same opinion. Last month, Mr. Haddad loved the main character, while Ines found her selfish. The club leader says this is the best part. “Each of us reads from a different perspective, shaped by our own lives,” she says. “So we each find different things in a book.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “perspective” mean?
options: a way of thinking shaped by your own experiences
the way far things look smaller in a drawing
a list of books to read
qs.why: Perspective is a way of thinking shaped by experience; the leader says it is “shaped by our own lives.” The drawing meaning does not fit here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “attends” mean?
qs.why: Attend means to go to an event or meeting regularly; the neighbors go to the club once a month.

qs.q: Why does the club leader like it when members disagree?
options: It helps them choose the next book
It means someone did not read the book
It proves that one person is right
Different life experiences help people find different things in a book
It makes Mr. Haddad change his mind
qs.why: She says each person reads from a perspective “shaped by our own lives,” so “we each find different things in a book.”

title: Where Is Biscuit?
text: On a windy Sunday, the gate blew open and Biscuit, the Okonkwo family's small brown dog, escaped into the street. Ade and his little sister Zara spent the whole afternoon searching the neighborhood. They looked under cars, behind stores, and in the park. Their mother told them not to worry, but she put signs on every corner. By dark, there was still no sign of Biscuit. Then, suddenly, Zara heard a familiar bark coming from the garden shed next door. Biscuit was hidden behind some old boxes, shaking and hungry. He had been afraid of the wind and had found a quiet place to wait.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “familiar” mean?
options: well known because she had heard it many times
qs.why: Familiar means well known from many times before; Zara knew her own dog’s bark. “Strange and new” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “hidden” mean?
options: out of sight, so he was hard to find
qs.why: Hidden means kept out of sight. Biscuit was behind boxes in the shed next door, not far from home.

qs.q: Why did Biscuit go into the shed?
options: He was afraid of the wind and wanted a quiet place
He wanted to play with the boxes
qs.why: The last sentence says he “had been afraid of the wind and had found a quiet place to wait.”

title: Friday Debate
text: In Ms. Rivera's class, students debate one question every Friday. This week the question was: “Should school start an hour later?” Ji-woo spoke first. She made a strong statement: “Teenagers need more sleep to learn well.” Then she showed proof from a study that found students who started later got better grades. Marcus objected. He said that a later start would mean later sports practice and less time for homework. Both sides spoke for five minutes. At the end, three students from another class judged the two sides. They decided Ji-woo's side had won, because she had used facts and not only feelings.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “objected” mean?
options: said that he did not agree
qs.why: Objected means said he did not agree. Marcus then gave reasons against a later start.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “proof” mean?
options: facts that show something is true
a first printed copy, used to check for mistakes
qs.why: Proof is facts or evidence that show something is true; Ji-woo used a study.

qs.q: Why did the judges choose Ji-woo's side?
options: She spoke for longer than Marcus
She supported her point with facts
qs.why: They decided she won “because she had used facts and not only feelings.” Both sides spoke for five minutes, and Marcus was the one who raised sports practice.

title: Market Day
text: Every Saturday morning, Ruth and Abdul Malik drive their truck to the farmers' market in the center of town. On their small farm, they produce vegetables, eggs, and honey. They bring a wide variety of food, from purple carrots to six kinds of tomatoes. At the market, consumers can buy directly from the farmers, without a store in the middle. This means the Maliks keep more of each dollar. The market gives them about half of their yearly income. Ruth also sells jam made with her grandmother's traditional recipe, which uses only fruit, sugar, and lemon.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “produce” mean?
qs.why: Produce here is a verb meaning to make or grow; the Maliks grow vegetables and get eggs and honey on their farm. “Fruit and vegetables” is the noun, which does not fit “they produce vegetables.”

qs.q: In the passage, what does “directly” mean?
qs.why: Directly means without going through another person or step; the passage explains “without a store in the middle.”

qs.q: Why do the Maliks keep more money when they sell at the market?
options: The market is free on Saturdays
They sell more food than any store
No store takes part of the money
qs.why: Buyers pay the farmers directly “without a store in the middle,” so the Maliks keep more of each dollar.

title: A Telescope in Space
